Show the difference between sort() and sorted().

Supplied answer
nums = [3, 1, 2]
new_list = sorted(nums) # returns a NEW list
print(nums, new_list) # [3, 1, 2] [1, 2, 3]
result = nums.sort() # changes nums, returns None
print(nums, result) # [1, 2, 3] None
Note: sort() works in place and returns None. sorted() returns a new sorted list.
